First, if you've previously earned a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards, you won't be able to earn another one for 48 months. Note that this is 48 months from the date you received your bonus, not from the date you were approved. In addition, if you previously earned a welcome bonus on the Capital One Venture X Rewards Credit Card, you will more than likely not be eligible to earn a welcome bonus on the Venture Rewards. Capital One may consider multiple factors when deciding whether to approve you; for a deeper dive into its application requirements, check out our full guide. Related: The best Capital One credit cards Earning Capital One miles This card earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on all purchases. So, by spending $4,000 on it to earn the welcome bonus, you'd earn at least 83,000 miles in the first few months, including the welcome bonus. And since the Venture Rewards earns 5 miles per dollar spent on car rentals, hotels and vacation rentals booked through Capital One Travel, it's possible to earn even more miles while working toward your welcome bonus. While some travel credit cards may earn slightly higher rates on select categories such as groceries or dining, the draw here is the simplicity and guarantee of earning at least 2 miles per dollar spent on anything you buy without the need to memorize multiple bonus spending categories. Related: Why I keep the Capital One Venture Rewards card in my wallet What can Capital One Miles get you? Your total value from this welcome bonus depends largely on how you redeem your miles. There are two key options: - Redeem for 1 cent apiece toward travel - Redeem by transferring to Capital One's 15-plus partner airlines and hotels (our recommendation) When converting your miles to hotel points or airline miles, most partners offer a 1:1 transfer ratio, though a couple of partners have different ratios. You can get great sweet spot redemptions by transferring miles to programs like Air Canada Aeroplan and Air France-KLM Flying Blue. For example, TPG's editor-in-chief, Nick Ewen, transferred 117,000 Capital One miles to Emirates Skywards to upgrade himself and two family members to Emirates first class. This broke down to 39,000 miles per person, a reasonable cost for the upgrade. If you don't want to transfer your miles, you can redeem them by booking a trip through Capital One Travel. These redemptions can be very handy in a world where you may be renting recreational vehicles, booking vacation home rentals or securing a cabin close to home more often than hopping on a flight to the other side of the world. Related: Cashing in Capital One miles? How to get the maximum value when redeeming miles Other Venture Rewards perks The Capital One Venture Rewards doesn't offer the same benefits as more premium travel rewards cards, including its upscale sibling, the Capital One Venture X Rewards. But for its modest $95 annual fee, the Venture Rewards provides some useful benefits: - An up to $120 statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fees - Car rental insurance - Complimentary concierge service - Extended warranty protection - No foreign transaction fees Related: Chase Sapphire Preferred Card vs. Capital One Venture Rewards Bottom line The Capital One Venture Rewards remains a strong option for travelers who value simplicity. It earns at least 2 miles per dollar spent on purchases and gives cardholders access to Capital One's airline and hotel transfer partners, all for a $95 annual fee. Plus, the current welcome offer includes a solid haul of miles and a $300 credit for Capital One Travel, one of the best offers we've seen. Just remember to use your credit in the first cardholder year, or you'll forfeit the value. To learn more, read our full review of the Capital One Venture Rewards card. Learn more: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card For Capital One products listed on this page, some of the benefits may be provided by Visa® or Mastercard® and may vary by product. See the respective Guide to Benefits for details, as terms and exclusions apply.

item.title: Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Which simple business cash-back card wins?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.50
Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Which simple business cash-back card wins? As a business owner myself, I've spent more brain power than I'd like to admit thinking about which credit cards can help me get more out of my business spending. Two cards that often come up when you're looking for a simple, no-annual-fee business card are the Ink Business Unlimited® Credit Card (see rates and fees) and Capital One Spark Cash Select — and it's easy to see why they're competitors. Both keep earning simple, offer tools and benefits for business owners and don't charge an annual fee. At the end of the day, though, the Ink Business Unlimited has an edge for most business owners, especially if you can pair it with an eligible Chase Ultimate Rewards card. I've already put more thought into business credit cards than any reasonable person should, so let me break it down for you. Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: At a glance | | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Annual fee | $0 | $0 | | Welcome bonus | Earn $1,000 cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months after account opening. | Earn a one-time $750 cash bonus after spending $6,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. | | Employee card fee | $0 | $0 | | Base earning rate | Unlimited 1.5% cash back | Unlimited 1.5% cash back | Quick picks by business type | Best for ... | Card | |---|---| | Business owners who already earn Chase Ultimate Rewards points | Ink Business Unlimited | | Those who want more time to finance a large purchase | Ink Business Unlimited | | Those who already earn Capital One miles | Capital One Spark Cash Select | | Those who make purchases abroad | Capital One Spark Cash Select | Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Welcome bonus The Ink Business Unlimited currently offers $1,000 cash back after spending $8,000 on purchases in the first four months after account opening. The Spark Cash Select offers a one-time $750 cash bonus after spending $6,000 on purchases within the first three months from account opening. The Ink's bonus is $250 higher, but you'll need to spend an additional $2,000 to earn it. If that level of spending is already normal for your business, the extra $250 is an easy win. But don't spend more than you otherwise would just to chase a bigger bonus. Eligibility is important to consider, too. Chase's application terms say the Ink Business Unlimited bonus may not be available if you've ever had this card or another no-annual-fee Chase business card. Meanwhile, Capital One states that the bonus may not be available to existing or previous Capital One Business cardholders. Winner: Ink Business Unlimited. Assuming you can comfortably meet the higher spending requirement, the extra $250 makes it the better offer. Related: The ultimate guide to credit card application restrictions Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select: Benefits Neither card is going to wow you with a long list of amazing perks — but that's hardly a surprise for a business card with no annual fee. However, both options offer more protection than you might expect, including extended warranty coverage and rental car insurance. | Benefit | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Employee cards | No additional cost | No additional cost | | Auto rental coverage | Primary for business rentals; up to $60,000 for most eligible vehicles | Primary for eligible business and international rentals* | | Purchase protection | Up to $10,000 per item for 120 days; $50,000 annual account limit | Up to $10,000 per item for 90 days; $50,000 annual account limit* | | Extended warranty protection | Adds one year to eligible warranties of three years or less | Doubles eligible warranties of 12 months or less, up to one additional year* | | Roadside assistance | Yes; cardholder pays for services | Yes; cardholder pays for services | | Foreign transaction fee | 3% | None | *Capital One Mastercard benefits are subject to issuer participation. Check your card's Guide to Benefits for applicable coverage. There's quite a bit of overlap between the two cards. Both offer extended warranty protection, purchase protection and rental car coverage, although the exact terms and coverage limits differ. The Ink Business Unlimited has an edge on purchase protection. Eligible purchases are covered against damage or theft for 120 days (up to $10,000 per item and $50,000 per account per year), whereas the Spark Cash Select only covers up to 90 days (with the same limits). The rental car comparison is closer than it first appears. Ink provides primary coverage when renting for business purposes, with reimbursement of up to $60,000 for theft and collision damage for most eligible vehicles. Depending on your card's applicable Mastercard benefits, Spark's MasterRental coverage can also be primary for eligible business rentals and rentals outside your home country. With primary coverage, you shouldn't have to file a claim with your personal auto insurer first. Spark, meanwhile, has an advantage if your business takes you abroad. It charges no foreign transaction fees, compared with 3% on the Ink Business Unlimited. Winner: Tie. Ink offers longer purchase protection and straightforward primary rental car coverage for eligible business rentals, while Spark counters with competitive protections and no foreign transaction fees. Related: Why nearly every purchase should be on a credit card How to earn and redeem rewards with the Ink Business Unlimited vs. Spark Cash Select At first glance, there's not much separating these cards when it comes to earning rewards. Both earn at least 1.5% back on everyday purchases, with no spending caps to track. | Purchase | Ink Business Unlimited | Capital One Spark Cash Select | |---|---|---| | Everyday purchases | 1.5% cash back | 1.5% cash back | | Lyft rides | 5% cash back through (Sept. 30, 2027) | 1.5% cash back | | Hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel | 1.5% cash back | 5% cash back | The Spark Cash Select has the edge on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel, earning 5% cash back. The Ink Business Unlimited has a 5% category for Lyft rides through (Sept. 30, 2027), but it's a temporary perk with a much narrower use case. Winner on earning: Spark Cash Select. Both cards earn the same 1.5% on everyday purchases, but Spark's 5% return on Capital One Business Travel bookings gives it a leg up. Redeeming rewards Cash back is the easiest way to use rewards with either card. But if you're willing to do a little more work, both cards have the potential to become much more useful for travel. You can convert the cash back you earn on the Ink Business Unlimited to points with an eligible Ultimate Rewards card, such as the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card (see rates and fees) or Chase Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ (see rates and fees). Doing so lets you transfer those points to Chase's airline and hotel partners. The Spark Cash Select works similarly. If you have an eligible Capital One miles-earning card, you can convert your cash back into Capital One miles and transfer those miles to Capital One's airline and hotel partners. Neither program is automatically better for travel, either. Chase and Capital One have different airline and hotel transfer partners, so the better option depends largely on which programs you actually use. If you already earn rewards with Chase or Capital One, that's an even stronger reason to stick with the same program and combine your rewards rather than starting from scratch with the other. Winner on redeeming: Tie. Both cards make cash back easy, while pairing either with an eligible card can open the door to transferable travel rewards. Related: How (and why) you should earn transferable credit card points Can I have both the Ink Business Unlimited and Spark Cash Select? Yes. Since one card is issued by Chase and the other by Capital One, there's nothing stopping you from holding both. But you'll still need to qualify for each card individually. For the Ink Business Unlimited, keep Chase's 5/24 rule in mind. You'll need to be under 5/24 to qualify, though most business cards won't count toward your 5/24 total. Capital One doesn't have a publicly stated rule comparable to Chase's 5/24 rule, but you'll still need to meet the issuer's current application requirements to qualify for the Spark Cash Select. But do you actually need both? Probably not. Since both earn at least 1.5% cash back on all purchases, there's a lot of overlap. And with several cash-back cards earning 2% on everyday spending, neither is the strongest choice based on its base earning rate alone. These cards are a better fit if you value simplicity, want to avoid an annual fee or already earn rewards with Chase or Capital One. But if you're starting from scratch, I'd look at options like the Wells Fargo Signify Business Cash® Card (see rates and fees), which earns 2% cash rewards on purchases, or the The American Express Blue Business Cash® Card, which earns 2% cash back on all eligible purchases (up to $50,000 per calendar year, then 1% back on all purchases). Related: The best business credit cards to add to your wallet Should I get the Ink Business Unlimited or Spark Cash Select? Choose the Ink Business Unlimited if you already have or want to get a Chase Ultimate Rewards-points earning credit card. Choose the Spark Cash Select if you regularly make international purchases or book hotels and rental cars through Capital One Business Travel. It's also a natural fit if you already have a Capital One travel card and can combine your rewards for more redemption options. Related: Your guide to the Chase Ink Business credit cards Bottom line After weighing it all, Chase's Ink Business Unlimited comes out ahead, but just barely. Its useful protections and the potential to get more from your rewards by pairing it with another Ultimate Rewards card give it the edge. Still, Capital One's Spark Cash Select puts up a good fight. With no foreign transaction fees and 5% back on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Business Travel, it could be the better fit for some business owners. To learn more, read our full review of the Ink Business Unlimited and our full review of the Capital One Spark Cash Select. Apply here: Ink Business Unlimited Credit Card Learn more: Capital One Spark Cash Select For Capital One products listed on this page, some of the benefits may be provided by Visa® or Mastercard® and may vary by product. See the respective Guide to Benefits for details, as terms and exclusions apply.

item.title: Better stays and bigger value with the Marriott Bonvoy American Express cards
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.50
Better stays and bigger value with the Marriott Bonvoy American Express cards There's a reason TPG awarded Marriott Bonvoy with Best Hotel Loyalty Program for two years and counting. Actually, there are several. With more than 30 brands and over 9,000 properties across the globe, you'll find exactly what you are looking for when you stay with Marriott, whether it's a luxury stay, a budget-friendly getaway or anything in between. When it comes to earning and redeeming points, Marriott Bonvoy's structure is surprisingly simple and lucrative. Marriott Bonvoy members earn up to 10 points per dollar spent on qualifying charges at hotels participating in Marriott Bonvoy, which can be redeemed for hotel stays and room upgrades, or transferred to more than 38 airline programs. And the perks you can get at Marriott Bonvoy's elite status tiers — like bonus points, space-available room upgrades, early check-in and late checkout (subject to availability) — add comfort and value to your stays when booked with a qualifying rate at hotels that participate in Marriott Bonvoy. Room upgrades are subject to availability upon check-in and only available to Gold and Platinum Elite members. Right now, you can earn even more points and get on the fast track to elite status with elevated welcome offers on two Marriott Bonvoy® American Express® Cards. These offers end Sept. 30, 2026, so let's take a look at how to choose the right card for your travel style. A top-tier card with premium benefits The Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card is the most premium card in the lineup, offering benefits that enhance not only your Marriott stays but also your everyday life. New Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant cardholders can earn 150,000 bonus points and a $250 statement credit after spending $6,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Offer ends Sept. 30. The Bonvoy Brilliant card has a $650 annual fee (see rates and fees), but when you combine the Bonvoy Brilliant's annual free night award (available upon annual card renewal, certain hotels have resort fees), which can be redeemed for up to 85,000 points per night at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels, and the annual $300 Brilliant Dining Credit (up to $25 in monthly statement credits for eligible dining purchases worldwide each calendar year), it's easy to get outsize value from the card before you even dip into the other benefits. Cardholders also get complimentary Marriott Bonvoy® Platinum Elite status, which includes benefits such as 50% bonus points on stays at participating brands, lounge access, room upgrades and late checkout. These benefits are subject to availability and apply only when a stay is booked at a qualifying rate at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels. You can earn up to a staggering 21 points per dollar spent on eligible purchases at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels on the card: 6 points for paying with the Bonvoy Brilliant card, up to 10 points for being a Marriott Bonvoy member and up to 5x points from Marriott Bonvoy on eligible hotel purchases with the 50% bonus points on stays benefit for Platinum Elite members. And with no foreign transaction fees (see rates and fees) and either a $120 statement credit for Global Entry or up to $85 for TSA PreCheck every four years, frequent travelers will reach for this card again and again. Whether you are a Marriott loyalist or only stay a few times each year, the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant card's complimentary Platinum Elite status, annual free night award (certain hotels have resort fees) and bonus points earning potential make it easy to take full advantage of its suite of benefits. And, if you apply by Sept. 30, you can earn 150,000 bonus points to use toward your next dream vacation. High earning potential for Marriott loyalists If you are looking for a lower annual fee or don't fancy yourself a frequent traveler, but still want to enjoy the benefits of elite status, the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card is a solid mid-tier option. The Bonvoy Bevy card has a $250 annual fee (see rates and fees), and new cardholders can earn 125,000 bonus points and a $150 statement credit after spending $5,000 on purchases in the first six months of card membership. Offer ends Sept. 30. Bonvoy Bevy cardholders get perks like a welcome gift of points when you stay at participating Marriott brands, automatic complimentary Marriott Bonvoy® Gold Elite status, complimentary room upgrades (subject to availability upon check-in) and a 2 p.m. late checkout (based on availability, when the stay is booked with a qualifying rate at hotels that participate in Marriott Bonvoy). You can also earn up to 18.5 Marriott Bonvoy points for every $1 spent on eligible purchases at participating Marriott Bonvoy hotels: 6 points for paying with the Bonvoy Bevy card, up to 10 points for being a Marriott Bonvoy member and up to 2.5 points with the 25% Bonus Points on Stays benefit for Gold Elite members. When you combine the bonus points you can earn on stays, plus the Bonvoy Bevy's 125,000-point welcome offer, you'll be on your way to points-fueled vacations in no time. Bottom line No matter which card you choose, it's clear that a Marriott Bonvoy American Express card is the upgrade your next trip needs. Learn more about the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant American Express Card and the Marriott Bonvoy Bevy American Express Card before these elevated offers end on Sept. 30. Learn more about the Marriott Bonvoy Brilliant® American Express® Card and Marriott Bonvoy Bevy® American Express® Card. For rates and fees of the American Express Bonvoy Brilliant, click here. For rates and fees of the American Express Bonvoy Bevy, click here. Terms apply to all offer and benefit mentions.

item.title: Best-ever offer: How good is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard 125K-mile bonus?
item.description:
Source: The Points Guy Score: 2.39
Best-ever offer: How good is the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard 125K-mile bonus? Editor's Note If you're serious about earning a ton of American Airlines AAdvantage miles and receiving elitelike benefits, the Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® (see rates and fees) likely deserves a spot in your wallet. The card recently received a refresh, adding new benefits while increasing its annual fee to $695. Beyond the welcome bonus, this card delivers real value through accelerated miles and Loyalty Points earning, a complimentary Admirals Club airport lounge membership, valuable statement credits, priority airport perks and inflight savings that can help offset that cost. With the card's welcome bonus now hitting the highest offer we've ever seen on this card — TPG readers are asking: How good is the Citi AAdvantage Executive limited time 125,000-mile offer, earned after spending $15,000 on purchases within the first five months from account opening? Here's my take on why this card remains so rewarding. How common is a 125,000‑mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive? Over the last seven years, the Citi / AAdvantage Executive reached the 100,000-mile mark only four times, making this new 125,000-mile offer truly exceptional. The previous high of 100,000 bonus miles was most recently offered in March of this year, and required spending $10,000 within the first three months from account opening (no longer available). The current offer requires more total spending — $15,000 instead of $10,000 — but gives you five months instead of three to meet the requirement. That works out to an average of $3,000 in monthly spending, compared with roughly $3,333 per month under the previous highest offer. So, while you'll need to spend an additional $5,000 overall, you have more time to do it and will earn an additional 25,000 AAdvantage miles. The last time the card hit 100,000 miles, it was available for less than three months. If you've been waiting for a reason to apply, this is it. Who is eligible for the 125,000‑mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive? To be approved for the Citi / AAdvantage Executive, a credit score of 670 or higher is recommended. Citi doesn't limit the total number of credit cards you can hold, but it does limit the overall credit line it will provide you. You can only apply for one card every eight days, and no more than two cards in 65 days. Citi's 48-month rule means you can't earn a welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive if you've received one on this card within the past four years. Note that the clock starts ticking from the time you receive the welcome bonus, not when you are approved for or activate the card. Related: The ultimate guide to credit card application restrictions How much are 125,000 AAdvantage miles worth? According to TPG's September 2026 valuations, AAdvantage miles are worth 1.45 cents each. That means the 125,000-mile welcome bonus on the Citi / AA Executive is worth an impressive $1,813. I'm drawn to AAdvantage miles for their flexibility and value. I like to use them for domestic American Airlines flights across the U.S., transatlantic trips to Europe, getaways to Mexico, and premium cabin redemptions on partner carriers like Finnair, Japan Airlines and Qantas. The AAdvantage program blends award chart and dynamic pricing models. When booking American Airlines or Fiji Airways flights, you'll encounter dynamic pricing where award costs fluctuate based on demand. But here's the sweet spot: most partner airlines operate under a fixed award chart with consistently reasonable rates, making them ideal for planning premium-cabin travel. Some top ways to maximize AAdvantage miles include flying: - Economy class domestically from just 7,500 miles, such as from Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW) to Philadelphia International Airport (PHL) - Economy class to Europe from 25,000 miles on a route like Charlotte Douglas International Airport (CLT) to Dublin Airport (DUB) - Business class from the U.S. to Helsinki Airport (HEL) on Finnair for 57,500 miles - Business class from the West Coast to Japan for 60,000 miles with Japan Airlines - Business class from the U.S. to Australia for 80,000 miles on Qantas Related: How to redeem American Airlines AAdvantage miles for maximum value So, is the 125,000-mile AAdvantage Executive offer one of the best deals ever? As someone who actively collects AAdvantage miles, which we value higher than Delta SkyMiles and United MileagePlus miles, this welcome offer definitely deserves serious consideration for anyone who flies with American Airlines or its partner airlines. The combination of the highest-ever bonus and the card's recent refresh makes this an especially compelling time to apply. Beyond the massive welcome bonus, here are the top five reasons to apply for this card: - Admirals Club membership: You'll get complimentary access to nearly 50 Admirals Clubs worldwide, plus 60-plus partner lounges, and can bring a spouse and children or two guests. This membership alone typically costs $750-$1,400 annually and more than covers the card's $695 fee. - Valuable travel credits: The card offers up to $500 annually in American Airlines Vacations statement credits, up to $180 in Lyft credits*, up to $120 in statement credits for eligible prepaid Avis or Budget car rentals and up to $100 in statement credits for eligible inflight and Admirals Club purchases. - Accelerated mile earning: You'll earn 12 miles per dollar spent on car rentals and hotels booked through American's travel platform, and 4 miles per dollar on eligible AA purchases. - Priority benefits: Save time and money with priority check-in and boarding (for you and up to eight companions, where available), plus complimentary first checked bag on domestic flights. - Elite status: You'll earn complimentary Champion status with Omni Hotels and Presidents Club status with Avis, plus qualify for Loyalty Point bonuses toward AAdvantage elite status. *Up to $15 per month after taking three eligible rides that month Bottom line The Citi / AAdvantage Executive is offering 125,000 bonus AAdvantage miles, the highest welcome offer we've ever tracked on the card. TPG values those miles at $1,813 (based on our valuations), making this a compelling offer for travelers who can comfortably meet the $15,000 spending requirement. Combined with a full Admirals Club membership (worth $750–$1,400 annually) and robust travel perks, the card pays for itself before you even book an award flight. And the redemption options are plentiful: fly domestically in the U.S. for as little as 7,500 miles, or use your AA miles to fly partner airlines like Japan Airlines, Qantas and Cathay Pacific, where fixed award charts make premium cabin bookings surprisingly affordable. Offers this generous don't stick around indefinitely. If you're a loyal American Airlines customer or regularly fly Oneworld carriers, this is the best time to apply. To learn more, check out our full review of the Citi / AAdvantage Executive Mastercard. Apply here: Citi / AAdvantage Executive World Legend Mastercard
